title: HF3022 (2017-2018 Regular): Firearm and ammunition transfer and eligibility to possess firearm provisions modified, certain firearm and firearm accessory possession prohibited or limited, and criminal penalties provided.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/90/2018/0/HF/3022/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Introduced version; no vote listed. Large file read via grep and section-by-section reading; quoted passages are those printed as new text in the saved version. The bracketed words in the Section 3 line are my summary, not quoted. The bill also strikes the old named-model list of 'semiautomatic military-style assault weapons' and replaces it with a features test (detachable magazine plus pistol grip, folding stock, etc.); expands pistol/assault-weapon transfer and eligibility rules to all firearms (sections 7, 13-29); makes firearm data private (section 1); redefines slide-fire stock as a trigger activator (section 6); sets owner grace periods (sections 34-35); and repeals the 609.66 subd. 1f transfer-without-check offence and other provisions (section 37). Penalty ladders in 624.7134 and 624.7135 are not quoted in full. The child-support part is a firearm rule, so treated as not a separate subject.

operative_text:
Section 30 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 2): It is unlawful for a person to manufacture, import, transfer, or possess an assault weapon.
Section 30 (Minn. Stat. 624.7134, subd. 4, para. (a)): A person who violates subdivision 2 is guilty of a felony and may be sentenced to imprisonment for not more than five years or to payment of a fine of not more than $25,000, or both.
Section 31 (Minn. Stat. 624.7135, subd. 2): It is unlawful for a person to manufacture, import, transfer, or possess a large-capacity magazine.
Section 10 (Minn. Stat. 624.712, subd. 14): "Large-capacity magazine" means any ammunition-feeding device with the capacity to accept more than ten rounds, or any conversion kit, part, or combination of parts from which this type of device can be assembled if those parts are in the possession or under the control of the same person.
Section 7 (Minn. Stat. 624.712, subd. 6): "Transfer" means a sale, gift, loan, assignment or other delivery to another, whether or not for consideration, of a firearm or the frame or receiver of a firearm.
Section 19 (Minn. Stat. 624.7132, subd. 1): Except as provided in this section, every person who agrees to transfer a firearm shall report the following information in writing to the chief of police of the organized full-time police department of the municipality where the proposed transferee resides or to the appropriate county sheriff if there is no such local chief of police:
Section 2 (Minn. Stat. 97B.031, subd. 4a): Except as provided in section 609.66, subdivision 1i, a person may not own or possess a silencer for a firearm or a firearm equipped to have a silencer attached.
Section 3 (Minn. Stat. 518A.681, para. (a)): [on the court's findings of child support or maintenance arrears of at least three times the monthly payments, or failure to comply with a subpoena] the court shall order that the obligor’s firearms rights be suspended.
Section 33 (Minn. Stat. 624.7161, subd. 4, para. (a)): A firearms dealer shall ensure that all ammunition is displayed behind a checkout counter where the public is not permitted and is offered for sale only by an employee who is at least 21 years of age and not prohibited by state or federal law from possessing a firearm.
Section 14 (Minn. Stat. 624.713, subd. 1a): A person presently charged with a crime punishable by imprisonment for a term exceeding one year shall not be entitled to receive, ship, or transport a firearm or ammunition.
